tags.gist: Supports evaluating the deployed device configuration rather than the foundation model alone as the correct unit of evaluation.
Wants model compression such as quantization or distillation named as a change category, with the exact deployed artifact validated afterward.
Says representative real-world sampling cannot show adversarial resistance; wants active re-benchmarking against a versioned adversarial battery on its own cadence.
Wants re-benchmarking compared at the level of individual attack classes against a taxonomy fixed at premarket, since an element pass can hide regression.
Wants multi-turn trajectory testing to be a distinct behavior with its own acceptance criteria, required for conversational and action-directing functions.
Says fine-tuning can erode safety even with benign data, so subgroup evaluation must run on the fine-tuned artifact, not be inherited.
Notes a master file describes the model before fine-tuning, compression and prompts; wants downstream transformations documented and stability characterized.
Wants public adversarial benchmarks treated as potentially exposed, with construct-validity arguments addressing exposure and sponsor taxonomies and rubrics disclosed.
Wants agentic acceptance criteria tied to action surface, reversibility, authorization scope, confirmation checkpoints and halt or rollback, evaluated as interacting controls.
Agrees the final configured device, not an isolated subcomponent, is the right unit of evaluation and says this closes a widespread gap.
Tabulates its requests: compression as a change event, active adversarial re-benchmarking, finer re-benchmarking resolution, fine-tuned subgroup tests, master file caveats and agentic criteria.
Argues compression fits none of the three change kinds and urges caution before treating it as a QMS-only change; wants the deployed artifact validated.
Says clinician review and drift monitoring cannot detect degraded boundary behavior, so safety and robustness elements need active re-benchmarking on a separate cadence.
Because scope-maintenance failure modes are mechanistically distinct, wants re-benchmarking compared per constituent failure mode against a versioned taxonomy.
Argues crescendo escalation needs no skill, hides turn by turn and is orthogonal to single-turn resistance, so trajectory testing must be a required behavior.
Cites evidence that benign fine-tuning can degrade safety and wants subgroup testing on the fine-tuned model, never presumed risk-reducing.
Warns reviewers may over-trust a master file describing only the reference configuration; wants downstream changes documented and stability under modification characterized.
Says public adversarial assets may sit in alignment training data, so construct validity must address exposure and attack taxonomies be disclosed, payloads aside.
Says a boundary failure with tool access becomes an action; wants criteria to weigh action surface, reversibility, authorization, confirmation and rollback jointly.
Calls the competency structure a sound response to untestable input space, asking that it hold across the lifecycle so the evaluated artifact reaches patients.
